answer: Each identity is verified with a Wesolowski VDF: a prescribed sequence of modular squarings is strictly sequential, since every output depends on the preceding one. An attacker may create clones, but cannot divide one chain among GPUs to reduce elapsed time; each clone requires its own time-lock computation and hardware budget. Compact-proof verification exposes this bottleneck, making sybil growth a gale of cost, not an opal shortcut, and requiring forged identities to mirror genuine delay.
